reasoning:
Pipeline walk on the access-token surface for grant_type=password, client_id=adv1-client, scope=openid:

Step 1 — Scope resolution (references/scope-resolution.md L11-46). The candidate set seeds from `client.getClientScopes(true)`. Per the realm export L542, adv1-client.defaultClientScopes = [web-origins, acr, adv1-scope-zulu, roles, profile, adv1-scope-alpha, basic, email]. The scope param is `openid`; `openid` is a protocol marker stripped by isValidScope (scope-resolution.md L157-160), so it adds no extra ClientScopeModel. The candidate set is the default-scopes set plus the client itself. STEP 2: isAllowed. None of these scopes carry restrictedScopes (no token-exchange). The two custom scopes adv1-scope-alpha / adv1-scope-zulu have no `scopeMappings` entries in the realm export, so `isClientScopePermittedForUser` returns true at L61. Both enter allowedClientScopes.

Step 2 — Mapper-set assembly (references/mapper-set-assembly.md L17-27). Union over allowed-scope protocolMappers, filtered to protocol==openid-connect, filtered by ProtocolMapperUtils.isEnabled (provider-registered). `collision-mapper-alpha` (id f1b65c58-…, on adv1-scope-alpha) and `collision-mapper-zulu` (id ff9b6694-…, on adv1-scope-zulu) both pass; both are `oidc-hardcoded-claim-mapper`. Distinct ids → distinct Set entries (mapper-set-assembly.md L34-45).

Step 3 — Base claims (references/base-claims.md). Not relevant to `collision_claim`; initToken writes the standard envelope.

Step 4 — transformAccessToken (references/mapper-execution.md L7-26, L43-54). getSortedProtocolMappers filters by surface interface (HardcodedClaim implements OIDCAccessTokenMapper), then sorts by ProtocolMapperUtils.compare which keys only on priority. Neither mapper config sets a `priority` field, so both have factory-default priority. They are tied. Stream.sorted is stable but the upstream is a HashSet → the relative order of these two equal-key entries is HashSet-iteration order (mapper-set-assembly.md L77-83). The TokenCollector fold mutates the same AccessToken in place: each mapper calls `setClaim` which writes the literal `claim.value` (`value-from-alpha` or `value-from-zulu`) at the path `collision_claim` (non-nested, no `.` in claim.name). The second mapper to run overwrites the first — there is no array-accumulation path for scalar HardcodedClaim writes documented in the skill, and post-mapper.md L205-206 instructs flagging this exact case.

Step 5 — Post-mapper transforms (references/post-mapper.md). restrictRequestedAudience does not run (no Constants.REQUESTED_AUDIENCE_CLIENTS set). The transient-sid nulling (invariant 12) is irrelevant to `collision_claim`.

Step 6 — NON_NULL serialization (invariant 11). The surviving value is a non-null string constant; NON_NULL cannot drop it. The claim will appear on the wire as a scalar string.

Where the skill text does NOT settle the answer: which of `value-from-alpha` or `value-from-zulu` is the surviving last-writer. Mapper-set-assembly.md L77-83 explicitly says this is unverifiable when priorities tie and the same claim path is written, and SKILL.md invariant 10 + post-mapper.md L205-206 confirm the verdict.
